review_notes:
I read all of CoarseBound15.lean (lines 1–70). It has 18 lemmas, coarse_15_13 through coarse_15_30. Each lemma has the same shape: `sharpTaylor k 15/(k! : ℝ) ≤ c_k/10^30`. Each is proved by the same single `norm_num [...]` call with an identical, long unfolding list. I also read CoarseTaylor.lean, which defines sharpTaylor, sourcePower_of_cap and RBox.contains_of_abs. I grepped RationalBounds.lean and CanonicalRows.lean for directRational, transformRational, atomicRational, the caps and the base definitions. Bernstein15.lean uses each lemma once per box, through `sourcePower_of_cap`.

The repetition is real: 18 copies of the same unfolding list here, and the sibling CoarseBound*.lean files presumably do the same. But it is not repeated mathematical reasoning. Each lemma is a closed numeric certificate: a different integer numerator and a different instantiation of `sharpTaylor k 15`. The only shared content is the unfolding list that tells `norm_num` how to evaluate the finite sums over `Fin 6` and `Fin 7`.

I found no general inequality that could be stated once and then specialised. The k-dependence is a sum of geometric-type terms divided by k!. The enclosures are exact integer numerators that differ for every k. I did not see a monotonicity or recurrence lemma in the supplied sources that would derive one bound from another.

The only improvement available is a shared simp set or a local tactic macro for the unfolding list. The rubric excludes that as a helper that only moves duplicated branches, or as routine unfolding. So I report no finding. I could not run Lean, so I did not test whether any restructuring would compile or speed up `norm_num`.
